title: improv·artist · gestural (Cy Twombly)
mutation_directive: improv artist: gestural via Cy Twombly

improv_extras.practice: scribble as handwriting; smeared chalk on cream; eros, mythology, illegibility

v1.feedback: The Twombly palette (graphite, blood red, umber on cream) is well-chosen and restrained, and the chalk-edge fragment shader is a nice touch. However, the piece is fundamentally a head scan with wiggly displacement — the 'gestural scribble' reads as jitter on a recognizable portrait, not as Twombly's actual practice of illegible mark-making where the scribble IS the subject. The trail lines are a good instinct but at 800 trails on a 55k-point head they get lost rather than reading as autonomous gestural marks. A stronger execution would dissolve the head silhouette more aggressively — let clusters of particles break free into looping calligraphic strokes that only loosely cohere into a face, so the tension between illegibility and recognition mirrors Twombly's tension between writing and drawing.

v2.feedback: The Twombly brief asks for scribble-as-handwriting and smeared chalk, but the piece reads more as a head dissolving into a particle cloud than as gestural calligraphic marks — the looping sine/cos paths produce uniform orbits, not the irregular, pressure-varying strokes Twombly's work demands. Replace the symmetric trig loops with polyline trail geometry or additive line segments that vary in width and opacity along their length, mimicking actual drawn marks. The palette is well-chosen (graphite, blood, umber, cream) but the uniform point-sprite rendering flattens it into a haze; elongated, directional sprites aligned to velocity would better evoke chalk drag. The head substrate is recognizable but risks the culled head-scan pattern — lean harder into illegibility by letting more clusters fully detach and trace autonomous scribble paths rather than hovering near the surface.
